The Damodar is the lifeline of the Bengal
The Damodar is a tributary of the Brahmaputra
explanation: The Damodar, the Sorrow of Bengal, was severely affected by the mining and the industrial pollution and the Damodar Valley Corporation was set up in 1947.

q: The 'Damodar Valley Corporation' was modelled on the:
options: The Ruhr valley of Germany
The Po valley of Italy
Tennessee Valley Authority of the USA
Murray-Darling basin of Australia
explanation: The Damodar Valley Corporation, set up in 1947, was modelled on the Tennessee Valley Authority of the United States.

options: The Mettur dam is on the Krishna
The Bhavani is a tributary of the Godavari
They are in Kerala
The Mettur dam is on the Kaveri and the Bhavani is its main tributary in the Tamil Nadu
explanation: The Mettur dam is on the Kaveri and the Bhavani, the Ponnai and the Noyyal are its tributaries in the Tamil Nadu.

options: The Papanasam, the Gadana and the Manimuthar are the tributaries of the Tambraparani
They are the tributaries of the Krishna
They are in Kerala
They are the tributaries of the Narmada
explanation: The Tambraparani, the main river of the Tirunelveli district, has the Papanasam, the Gadana, the Manimuthar and the Ganga as its tributaries.

options: The Son is in Kerala
The Son is the largest tributary of the Ganga by the discharge and the Sone is the same river
The Son is a tributary of the Godavari
The Son is a tributary of the Krishna
explanation: The Son or the Sone, the largest tributary of the Ganga by the discharge, rises in the Amarkantak and it joins the Ganga near Patna with the Gandak and the Kosi.

options: The Hooghly is a tributary of the Brahmaputra
The Hooghly flows into the Arabian Sea
The Hooghly is a natural lake
The Hugli and the Bhagirathi have become the Hooghly, the distributary that flows past Kolkata
explanation: The Hugli, the Bhagirathi and the Ganga together form the Hooghly, the distributary that flows past Kolkata and the Haldia and the Paradip are the river ports.

q: The 'Ganga' and the 'Rajmahal' and the 'Rajmahal hills':
options: The Rajmahal hills are of the Deccan trap
The Ganga cuts a gorge through the Rajmahal hills, which is a volcanic formation
The Rajmahal hills are in the Himalaya
The Ganga does not pass the Rajmahal hills
explanation: The Ganga cuts a dramatic gorge through the volcanic Rajmahal hills in Bihar and the Sarauni and the Rajmahal are the important passes there.

options: The Farakka Barrage diverts the Ganga to the Hooghly to flush the silt and to keep the navigation open
The Farakka Barrage supplies the irrigation to the Punjab
The Farakka Barrage is on the Brahmaputra
The Farakka Barrage is a hydroelectric project
explanation: The Farakka Barrage, completed in 1975, diverts the Ganga to the Bhagirathi-Hooghly to flush the silt and to maintain the navigability of the Calcutta port.

options: The Narmada valley is in the Deccan plateau
The Narmada valley is in the Aravalli
The Narmada valley in the Bori and the Betasia is a part of the Satpura and the Maikala
The Narmada valley is in the Himalaya
explanation: The Narmada valley in the Bori and the Betasia hills is a part of the rugged Satpura and the Maikala ranges and the Narmada cuts through it in a rift.

options: They are the rivers of the Deccan
They are the rivers of the Kaveri valley
The Ganga and the Damodar and the Karkhardanga are the rivers of the Chota Nagpur
They are the rivers of the Himalaya
explanation: The Damodar, the Subarnarekha and the North and the South Koel are the rivers of the Chota Nagpur and the Karkhardanga is a tributary of the Subarnarekha.

options: The Teesta is a tributary of the Ganga
The Teesta is in Kerala
The Teesta flows into the Arabian Sea
The Teesta, the Tista, is a tributary of the Brahmaputra and it flows through the Sikkim and the Jalpaiguri
explanation: The Teesta, or the Tista, is a tributary of the Brahmaputra that flows through the Sikkim and the Jalpaiguri district and it caused the 1892 and the 1964 floods in the plains of West Bengal.

options: The Kalimpong hills are in Tamil Nadu
The Teesta and the Kalimpong hills and the Siliguri corridor are in the Himalayan belt of West Bengal
The Teesta is in Kerala
The Siliguri corridor is in Rajasthan
explanation: The Teesta, the Kalimpong hills and the Siliguri corridor are the Himalayan features of West Bengal, and the Siliguri corridor is the narrow link to the North-East.

q: The 'Ganga' and the 'Hugli' and the 'Ganges delta':
options: The Bengal delta is the largest delta in the world with the Sundarbans
The Bengal delta is the smallest delta
There is no delta in India
The delta is in the Deccan
explanation: The Bengal delta, with the Sundarbans, is the largest delta in the world and it is the most populous delta as well.

options: The Indus valley is in the Tamil Nadu
The Indus valley civilisation is named after the Indus and it extends to the Punjab and the Sindh
The Indus valley is in the Bengal
The Indus valley is in the Deccan
explanation: The Indus valley civilisation, also called the Harappan civilisation, took its name from the Indus and it extended to the Punjab and the Sindh in Pakistan and to the Haryana and the Punjab in India.

options: The Ghaggar and the Hakra, the ancient tributaries of the Indus, are identified with the Saraswati
They are the tributaries of the Ganga
They are in the Deccan
They are the tributaries of the Kaveri
explanation: The Ghaggar and the Hakra, the ancient tributaries of the Indus that are identified with the Saraswati of the Vedic age, dried up with the climatic changes.

options: They are in Rajasthan
They are the west flowing rivers of the Deccan
The Sutlej, the Beas and the Ravi are the five rivers of the Indus system that flow through Punjab
They are the tributaries of the Ganga
explanation: The five rivers of the Indus system are the Jhelum, the Chenab, the Ravi, the Beas and the Sutlej, of which the last three flow through Punjab.

options: They are the dams of the Bhakra
They are the barrages of the Ganga
They are the pumping stations of the Bhakra
The Madhopur and the Sukhsar headworks are the diversion works of the Indira Gandhi Canal
explanation: The Madhopur and the Sukhsar headworks at the Harike Barrage are the diversion works that feed the Indira Gandhi Canal.

q: In the context of the Punjab, which of the following is correct?
options: The Punjab is a desert region
The Ghaggar flows into the Bay of Bengal
The Punjab is in the Deccan
The Punjab is the land of the five rivers and the Ghaggar was the Saraswati of the Vedic age
explanation: The Punjab is the land of the five rivers and the Ghaggar, the largest of them in the Vedic period, is identified with the Saraswati.

q: The 'Ram Ganga' and the 'Ganga' and the 'Uttarakhand':
options: The Ram Ganga rises in the Garhwal hills and the projects at Kalagarh and the Upper Ganga Canal irrigate western Uttar Pradesh
The Ram Ganga rises in the Himalaya of Nepal
The Ram Ganga is a tributary of the Godavari
The Ram Ganga flows west into the Arabian Sea
explanation: The Ram Ganga rises in the Garhwal hills and the Upper Ganga Canal takes off from the Ramganga barrage at Kalagarh to irrigate the western Uttar Pradesh.

q: The 'Ganga' and the 'Son' and the 'Sone' and the 'Bihar':
options: The Son flows into the Arabian Sea
The Son, the Sone, the Gandak and the Kosi are the rivers that make the north Bihar plain
The Son is a tributary of the Krishna
The Son is in Kerala
explanation: The Son, the Gandak and the Kosi, with their tributaries, form the alluvial plain of north Bihar, which is among the most fertile in the world.

options: The Kosi is the longest river of the Deccan
The Kosi flows west
The Kosi brings the alluvium that forms the Saharsa and the Kosi divisions
The Kosi is in Kerala
explanation: The Kosi, with its tributaries, brings the enormous alluvial deposits that form the Saharsa and the Kosi divisions of north Bihar.

options: The Farakka is in Kerala
The Teesta and the Farakka barrage control the flow of the Ganga into the Hooghly
The Farakka diverts the Ganga into the Brahmaputra
The Teesta is a tributary of the Krishna
explanation: The Farakka and the Teesta barrages regulate the diversion of the Ganga and the Teesta into the Hooghly and they are vital to the navigation of the Calcutta port.

options: a concentration of the Bhil, the Bhilala, the Barda and the Gond tribes
in the Deccan
in the Himalaya
no tribal population
explanation: The Narmada valley has a high concentration of the Bhil, the Bhilala, the Barda and the Gond and the Baghel and the Korku tribes.

q: The 'Betwa' and the 'Ken' and the 'Tons' and the 'Tawa':
options: The Tawa dam is in Kerala
The Tawa dam is on the Ken
The Tawa dam is on the Tawa, a tributary of the Betwa, in Madhya Pradesh
The Tawa dam is on the Tapti
explanation: The Tawa dam is on the Tawa river, a tributary of the Betwa, in the Betwa project complex in Madhya Pradesh.

options: They are the tributaries of the Krishna in Andhra
They are the tributaries of the Kaveri
They are in Kerala
The Bhadra, the Varahi, the Kadam and the Aghanashini are the tributaries of the Tungabhadra
explanation: The Tungabhadra is the chief tributary of the Krishna and the Bhadra, the Varahi, the Kadam and the Aghanashini are its tributaries.

options: The Bhima is a tributary of the Godavari
The Bhima flows into the Arabian Sea
The Bhima rises in the Himalaya of Nepal
The Bhima is a tributary of the Krishna that flows through Maharashtra and the Kabini is a tributary of the Kaveri
explanation: The Bhima, about 861 km long, is a tributary of the Krishna and it flows through Maharashtra and the Purna is its chief tributary.

options: They are the tributaries of the Kaveri
They are in Kerala
The Pravara and the Purna are the chief tributaries of the Godavari
They are the tributaries of the Krishna
explanation: The Pravara, the Purna, the Manjira and the Indravati are the chief tributaries of the Godavari and the Godavari basin is the largest of the peninsular India.

options: They are in Tamil Nadu
The Kabini and the Lakshmantirth are the tributaries of the Kaveri
They are the tributaries of the Krishna
They are the tributaries of the Godavari
explanation: The Kabini, the Hemavati, the Shivasamudram or the Lakshmantirth and the Noyyal are the tributaries of the Kaveri in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the Narmada is correct?
options: The Bhils are the largest of the tribal communities of the Narmada valley
The Bhils are the largest of the Mizo tribes
The Bhils are of the Himalayan belt
The Bhils are the pastoral tribes of the Ladakh
explanation: The Bhils, with about 1.7 million people, are the largest of the tribal communities of the Narmada valley and they are the pastoral nomads of the Western Ghats.

q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in relation to the Krishna?
options: The Krishna and the Godavari form the largest delta of the eastern coast
The Krishna forms a delta with the Kaveri
The Krishna forms a delta with the Tapti
There is no delta of the Krishna
explanation: The Krishna and the Godavari together form the largest delta on the eastern coast and the Nagarjuna Sagar project was a pioneering river valley project.

q: The Gandhi Sagar and the Kota Barrage are:
options: on the Son
on the Chambal
on the Narmada
on the Betwa
explanation: The Jawahar Sagar, the Gandhi Sagar and the Kota Barrage are the three stages of the Chambal Valley Project in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.

options: the site of the first project in the north
no projects
the site of the Bhakra project
the site of the first major multipurpose project in the south
explanation: The Krishna valley with the Nagarjuna Sagar, the Srisailam and the Pochampadu projects was the site of the pioneering river valley development in the south.

options: on the Brahmaputra
for the irrigation
to be a permanent solution but the silt led to the construction of the Bhagirathi-Hooghly scheme
never built
explanation: The Farakka barrage was to divert the Ganga to the Hooghly, but the silting made the scheme ineffective and the linking of the Ganga with the Bhagirathi was needed.

options: a national park only
in Bangladesh only
a desert
the largest mangrove forest and it is a biosphere reserve and a Ramsar site and a World Heritage site
explanation: The Sundarbans is a national park in West Bengal and it is a biosphere reserve, a Ramsar site and a UNESCO World Heritage site, and it is the habitat of the Royal Bengal tiger.

options: a fresh water delta
in Tamil Nadu
the largest in the world and it is the home of the Royal Bengal tiger
in Kerala
explanation: The Sundarban delta, the largest in the world, is the home of the Royal Bengal tiger and it is the most important mangrove region of the earth.

q: The Gandak and the Kosi and the Ghaghara and the Saryu are:
options: the rivers of the northern plain
the rivers of the Deccan
the rivers of the Western Ghats
the rivers of the Ladakh
explanation: The Gandak, the Kosi, the Ghaghara and the Saryu and their tributaries form the northern plain of the Ganga and they bring the alluvium of the Shillong Plateau.

q: Consider the following statements. Which of them is correct with regard to the Ganga?
options: The Rajmahal hills are the highest of the peninsula
The Rajmahal hills of the volcanic origin rise in the middle of the Ganga course
The Rajmahal hills are of the Himalayan origin
The Rajmahal hills are in Kerala
explanation: The Rajmahal hills, of the volcanic origin and about 400 metres high, rise in the middle of the course of the Ganga and the Ganga cuts a deep gorge through them.

options: the industrial belt of eastern India with the DVC and the Bokaro
in Kerala
the iron ore of the Bellary
the tea belt of Assam
explanation: The Damodar valley of the Chota Nagpur plateau is the industrial belt of eastern India with the Bokaro steel plant, the Durgapur steel plant and the coal fields.

q: The Son and the Kosi bring the alluvium that makes:
options: they bring the alluvium of the Deccan
the west flowing rivers of the peninsula
the rivers of the Rajasthan
the north Bihar plain fertile
explanation: The Son, the Gandak and the Kosi, with their tributaries, have created the fertile alluvial plain of north Bihar.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the Teesta is correct?
options: The Teesta is in Kerala
The Teesta flows west into the Arabian Sea
The Teesta flows through the Jalpaiguri district of West Bengal and causes the floods
The Teesta is a tributary of the Godavari
explanation: The Teesta flows through the Jalpaiguri and the Cooch Behar districts and it is the most devastating river of West Bengal with its floods.

options: is in Kerala
flows through the Rewa, the Palamu and the Rajmahal hills
is a tributary of the Krishna
flows into the Arabian Sea
explanation: The Son rises at Amarkantak and flows through the Rewa, Palamu and Rohtas districts and the Rajmahal hills before joining the Ganga. It is a tributary of the Ganga and not of the Krishna.

q: The Jonk and the Sonakhan are:
options: a tributary of the Krishna
a tributary of the Kaveri
in Kerala
the chief tributaries of the Mahanadi
explanation: The Jonk and the Sonakhan are the chief tributaries of the Mahanadi and the upper course of the Mahanadi in the Dandakaranya is called the Kolab or the Kanger.

options: the highest of the Deccan
in the Madhya Pradesh and the Amarkantak plateau is the highest of the Satpura
in the Himalaya
in Kerala
explanation: The Maikala range forms the boundary of the Madhya Pradesh and the Amarkantak plateau, the highest part of the Satpura, is the source of the Narmada.

q: Consider the following statements. Which of them is correct with regard to the Krishna rises at the Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats and the valley?
options: The Krishna rises in the Deccan trap
The Krishna rises at the Amarkantak
The Krishna rises at the Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats and the valley is the granitic core of the Ghats
The Mahabaleshwar is in the Himalaya
explanation: The Krishna rises at the Mahabaleshwar in the high granitic core of the Western Ghats and the highly dissected valley is a popular hill station.

q: In the context of the Tungabhadra, which of the following is correct?
options: The Hampi is the ruined capital of the Vijayanagara on the Tungabhadra
The Hampi is in Kerala
The Hampi is a hill station of the Deccan
The Hampi is on the Kaveri
explanation: The Hampi, the ruined capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, stands on the banks of the Tungabhadra and it is a World Heritage site.

q: The Indus and the Shyok are:
options: a river of Kerala
The Indus flows through the Gangetic plain
the longest river of the Himalaya
the rivers of the Ladakh and the Gilgit region
explanation: The Indus and the Shyok flow through the cold desert of Ladakh and the Gilgit-Baltistan, and the upper Indus is the lifeline of the Gilgit and the Ladakh.

q: The Nubra and the Surlej are:
options: in Kerala
a west flowing river of the Deccan
the tributaries of the Indus in Ladakh
a tributary of the Ganga
explanation: The Nubra and the Surlej are the tributaries of the Indus in the Nubra valley of Ladakh and the Shyok is the other important one.

q: In the context of the Ramganga, which of the following is correct?
options: The Tehri dam is on the Son
The Tehri dam is on the Bhagirathi, a tributary of the Ganga
The Tehri dam is on the Tapti
The Tehri dam is on the Sutlej
explanation: The Tehri dam, the highest in India, is on the Bhagirathi, a tributary of the Ganga, and the water is released through the Tehri Canal to the Ganga.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the The Rihand is correct?
options: The Rihand is the largest tributary of the Son and the Rihand joins the Son at the boundary of the Chhattisgarh and the Uttar Pradesh
The Rihand is a tributary of the Krishna
The Rihand is in Kerala
The Rihand flows west
explanation: The Rihand, the largest tributary of the Son, joins the Son at the tri-junction of the Madhya Pradesh, the Chhattisgarh and the Uttar Pradesh.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the The Sind is correct?
options: The Sind is the largest tributary of the Chambal in the lower course
The Sind is a tributary of the Krishna
The Sind is in Kerala
The Sind flows into the Arabian Sea
explanation: The Sind, the largest tributary of the Chambal, joins the main river on the boundary of the Madhya Pradesh and the Rajasthan.

q: The Kali, the Bedti and the Varahi are:
options: the rivers of Kerala
the tributaries of the Godavari
the west flowing rivers of the Western Ghats in Karnataka
the east flowing rivers of Karnataka
explanation: The Kali, the Bedti and the Varahi are the principal west flowing rivers of the Western Ghats in Karnataka and the Varahi is the Varahi or the Bedti that forms the Kali.

q: The Ayyankovil and the Pamba are:
options: in Tamil Nadu
the rivers of the Kuttanad and the Malabar
the rivers of the Deccan
the tributaries of the Krishna
explanation: The Pamba and the Ayyankovil are the rivers of the Malabar region and the Pamba is the river that enters the Kuttanad.

q: The Bharathapuzha and the Chaliyar are:
options: the rivers of the Deccan
the tributaries of the Krishna
in Tamil Nadu
the rivers that reach the coast at the Malappuram and the Kannur
explanation: The Bharathapuzha reaches the sea at the Ponnani in the Malappuram and the Chaliyar at the Koduvally in the Kannur.

q: The Barna and the Betwa are:
options: the tributaries of the Narmada in the Central India
the tributaries of the Krishna
in Kerala
the rivers of the Ladakh
explanation: The Barna and the Betwa are the tributaries of the Narmada and the Narmada is the only west flowing river of peninsular India with a large catchment.
